html:
SMTO-EXE-0182 — SMTO doesn't know if your new document was saved

GUID: 2f85082e-a8a1-52d7-aec1-49c2915b5cc8
Slug: office-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway (the helper program that works with files on a computer) to save a new copy of your document, but never got a clear answer back. The new copy may or may not exist. Your original file wasn't replaced.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts under SMTO's reply in this task, and look in any folder you asked SMTO to save to, for a new copy of the document created just now. The save may have finished even though SMTO didn't hear back, so the file could already be there.
  2. If you find the new copy, open it and check that it contains the change you asked for. A copy that looks complete means the step worked and nothing needs repeating.
  3. Only if there is no new copy, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, make sure the Gateway shows as connected, then ask SMTO to do the step again. A lost connection to the Gateway is a common reason the answer never arrived.

What success looks like

  • You have exactly one new copy of the document with your change, and the Gateway shows as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and folder, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the change before checking for a new copy, or you may end up with duplicates.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An Office write lost its result: the Gateway changed the destination before an exception, or the server received an invalid or no response, so the output outcome cannot be established.

What this means

  • Publication may have changed the destination before an exception, or a write lost its valid transport receipt; the runtime cannot establish the complete output outcome. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Publication may have changed the destination before an exception, or a write lost its valid transport receipt; the runtime cannot establish the complete output outcome.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact intended output path and run artifacts together with the original receipt and source revision.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the write. Inspect the requested output_path on the selected Gateway and the run's artifact directory (artifact-workspace://) for a file created by this execution, verify its contents, and only then decide whether a new, separately approved write is needed; also check Gateway connectivity and logs for the lost response.
  • Inspect the selected output path and run artifacts before deciding on another mutation; never automatically replay the write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the selected output path and run artifacts before deciding on another mutation; never automatically replay the write.

How to verify the fix

  • The original publication is reconciled before any replacement or repeated output write.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
